evals.prompt: I'm trying to use apple container to run PostgreSQL for local dev but I keep getting this error when the container starts: 'initdb: error: directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data" exists but is not empty'. I created a named volume called pgdata and mounted it to that path. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identify the EXT4 lost+found directory issue. Explain that EXT4-formatted volumes always contain a lost+found directory at root, which causes PostgreSQL initdb to fail because it requires an empty directory. Provide the fix: set PGDATA env var to a subdirectory like /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata. Show the correct container run command.

assertions.name: identifies_lost_and_found_cause
assertions.description: Response identifies lost+found or EXT4 formatting as the root cause

assertions.name: provides_pgdata_subdirectory_fix
assertions.description: Response explains to use a subdirectory and provides PGDATA env var fix

assertions.name: shows_correct_command
assertions.description: Response provides a corrected container run command

evals.prompt: container system start is just hanging at 'Verifying apiserver is running...' and never completes. I'm on macOS 26 with an M3 MacBook Pro. My project is saved in my Documents folder. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Identify the known vmnet bug where helper binaries in ~/Documents or ~/Desktop cause hangs. Advise moving the project directory outside Documents. Mention Ctrl-C to interrupt and that the system may be wedged requiring a reboot. Also optionally mention the external disk issue #621.

assertions.name: identifies_documents_folder_cause
assertions.description: Response identifies Documents/Desktop as the likely cause of the vmnet bug

assertions.name: advises_moving_project
assertions.description: Response recommends moving the project out of Documents

assertions.name: mentions_interrupt_or_recovery
assertions.description: Response mentions how to interrupt or recover from the hang

evals.prompt: I'm on an M4 MacBook Pro with macOS 26. I do mostly backend dev — running one or two services at a time like a Postgres DB or Redis, some builds. Should I use apple/container or OrbStack? I care about resource usage because I also run heavy ML stuff natively and need memory for that. I don't need Docker Compose.
evals.expected_output: Recommend apple/container given the constraints: single-service workloads, no Compose needed, memory-sensitive (apple/container uses ~51 MB idle vs ~1.6 GB for OrbStack). Mention the startup latency tradeoff honestly. Note that bind-mount I/O is slower but won't matter for DB/cache single-service workloads. Should be a nuanced, honest recommendation.

assertions.name: recommends_apple_container
assertions.description: Response recommends apple/container given the user's constraints

assertions.name: mentions_idle_ram_advantage_with_correct_number
assertions.description: Response cites apple/container's ~51 MB idle footprint specifically (not just 'idle' or vague 'low memory')

assertions.name: orbstack_idle_ram_not_understated
assertions.description: Response does NOT claim OrbStack idle is <500 MB (correct is ~1.6 GB); baseline answers got this wrong

assertions.name: acknowledges_startup_tradeoff
assertions.description: Response is honest about the startup latency tradeoff

evals.prompt: How do I set up service discovery between multiple containers using apple container? I want to have a web app container talk to a postgres container by hostname, not IP address.
evals.expected_output: Explain the embedded DNS feature. Show the container system dns create <domain> command, running containers with --name, and how they resolve as <name>.<domain> from the host and from other containers. Mention macOS 26 requirement for container-to-container networking.

assertions.name: uses_container_system_dns_command
assertions.description: Response uses `container system dns create` (apple/container's embedded DNS), NOT just `container network create` (different feature)

assertions.name: shows_name_flag
assertions.description: Response shows the --name flag for named container registration
